1: [Masnavi, Book I — The song of the reed]

Listen to the reed, how it tells a tale of separations. Ever since I was cut from the reed-bed, men and women have wept at my cry. I want a heart torn open with longing, so that I may tell the pain of desire — for everyone who is far from his source longs to return to it.
[Masnavi, Book I — The elephant in the dark]

The elephant was in a dark house, and those who saw it had never seen one. One felt its trunk and said: It is like a water-spout. One felt its ear: a fan. One its leg: a pillar. One its back: a throne. Each was right in his part and wrong in his whole — and the house is the world, and the lamp we carry is so small, and the elephant is so large.

This being human is a guest house: every morning a new arrival — a joy, a depression, a meanness, some momentary awareness comes as an unexpected visitor. Welcome and entertain them all! Even if they are a crowd of sorrows, who violently sweep your house empty of its furniture, still treat each guest honourably. He may be clearing you out for some new delight.
2: [Masnavi, Book I — The merchant and the parrot]

A merchant going to India asked his caged parrot what gift it wanted. Bring me the freedom of the birds of the forest, said the parrot. In India the merchant saw the parrots, and called out: A prisoner among you longs for freedom. And the wild parrots fell down dead — and his own parrot, seeing it, fell dead too. Grieving, he threw the body out — and the parrot rose and flew, saying: That was the teaching: feign death to be free.
[Masnavi, Book I — The way of the heart]

The way of the religion of love is other than all ways. Whether the beloved is Muslim or unbeliever, love is not bound by the names we give it. The lovers have no creed but the beloved, and no scripture but the face, and no pilgrimage but the turning.

A woman dreamed that the Prophet came to her and said: My teaching is in three things — to keep the tongue from the fault of others, to keep the heart from envy, and to keep the eyes from the fault you are about to excuse in yourself. And she woke, and wrote it down, and the writing is still warm.
3: A jug was carried to the river to be filled, and the river asked it: Why do you tremble? The jug said: I am afraid you will break me. The river said: I was a jug once, and I was broken, and I have been the river ever since — and every drop of me is still the river, and every drop of you is still the sea, and the breaking is the return.
[Masnavi, Book II — The work of the saints]

The saints are the physicians of the world, and their medicine is presence. They do not argue with the sick; they sit by them. They do not promise the road is short; they walk it beside you. And the sick, in the end, are healed less by the remedy than by the sitting.

There is a way between the worlds that is not on any map, and the travellers on it do not carry provisions, for they eat the distance. Their luggage is a name — one name, the Beloved's — and at every border the name is the passport, and the gates open, and the guards bow, for they too are travelling, and they too know the name.
